label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
**Statement of Driver**

Date: November 11, 2026

To: Mrs. Okafor
Copy to: Transportation Office, Attn: Darlene [last name], Supervisor; driver file

Re: Complaint dated October 29, 2026. Bus 41, Route 9, Tuesday, October 27, 2026, afternoon run

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

My name is [Your Name], and I am the driver of Bus 41. I have been a school bus driver for 28 years, and I drive your daughter Amara every day. I was asked by my supervisor to give my account of what happened on October 27, and since you will be reading this, I am writing it to you directly. I want you to know exactly what happened and why.

**What happened**

On Tuesday, October 27, I arrived at Amara's stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street at 3:52 p.m. The schedule has us there at 3:50. Amara is a kindergarten student at Fairmont Elementary, and she has the green tag on her bag. That tag means an adult must be at the stop to receive her before she can get off the bus.

I looked at the stop and did not see an adult at the corner. I waited until about 3:55. Still nobody I could see. At 3:56 I radioed dispatch and spoke with Gloria, who called the school. I had three more stops to make and 14 children still on the bus.

The district rule for kindergarten riders is that if no adult is at the stop, the child stays on the bus and is returned to the school, and the school office calls the parent. That is what I did. I am not allowed to let a kindergartner off without an adult there, and I would not have felt right doing it even if I were allowed.

I finished the rest of my route and brought Amara back to Fairmont at 4:31 p.m. I walked her inside myself and handed her to Mrs. Petrakis in the office.

**About Amara**

I know the most important thing to you is how your daughter was. Amara was fine the whole time. She was coloring on her folder. At one point she asked me if she could ride some more, and I told her we were going on a little extra trip. I did not want her worried, and she did not seem to be.

**What I understand you saw**

I have read that you told the office you were parked across Brandt Street by the laundromat, that you waved, and that I did not respond. I believe you that you were there. But I did not see you. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street, and from the driver's seat I could not see past it. If I had seen you, I would have stopped and sorted it out right there.

I also want to answer the statement that I "drove off laughing." I was not laughing. As we were pulling away from the stop, I was telling a fourth grader in seat 2 to sit back down. If I looked like I was smiling or talking, that is what it was. I would never laugh at a situation like this, and I understand how it must have looked to someone watching from across the road.

I also want to say something about the word "took." I understand why it felt that way to you. You watched the bus leave with your five-year-old on it and no explanation. But I was not taking her anywhere other than to the one place the district tells us to bring her, where there are staff who would call you right away. I know that doesn't make it any less frightening when you are standing there. I have grandkids of my own, and I would have been scared too.

**Why I could not get off the bus**

I was not able to leave the bus and walk across the street to look for a parent. I had 14 children on board, and I cannot leave them unattended. That is not something I will do. So I depended on what I could see from the driver's seat, and what I could see was an empty corner.

**Request for the camera footage**

I am asking the Transportation Office to pull the video from the camera on Bus 41 for the afternoon of October 27. It should show the stop, the time I arrived, how long I waited, and what was and was not visible from the bus. I would like that footage reviewed and made part of the file. I believe it will show that I waited, followed the procedure, and did not leave early.

**What I am asking going forward**

I would like this to go better for you and for Amara, and I have one simple request. When you are meeting the bus, please stand on the bus side of the street, near the corner where I stop, or step out of your car so that I can see you. If I can see an adult, Amara gets off the bus. If you are going to be late, or if someone else will be meeting her, a call to the transportation office or her school ahead of time lets us know and keeps this from happening again.

I also want to be honest about one thing. I am not going to apologize for following the rule, because I was doing what I am required to do to keep her safe. But I am sorry that Amara's afternoon went the way it did, and I am sorry for the fright and worry it caused you.

**Closing**

I have been doing this job for 28 years without a write-up, and this is a job I take seriously. Several years ago a similar thing happened on my route with a different family, and they thanked me afterward. I am not saying that to compare, only to say that I do this the same way every time, for every child.

I am glad to keep driving Amara. She is a sweet girl, and I want her to feel safe on my bus. I want to get this fixed so that you can feel comfortable about it too. If you would like to talk with me, I am happy to do that through Darlene or the Transportation Office.

Respectfully,

[Your Name]
Bus Driver, Bus 41, Route 9
[Phone or contact info if you want it included]

---

A few notes: I put in your date as November 11, so change it if you sign it on a different day. Fill in your name and Darlene's last name. Since the statement goes to Mrs. Okafor, I left off any contact info beyond what you choose to add, so decide whether you want your phone number on it. It's about 950 words, well within your limit.
